memory_update.text: AMKR should be retained as the US-listed reference OSAT anchor for advanced packaging and test overflow; verify AI/HPC-specific revenue mix and capacity ramp timing before upgrading beyond reference context.
CAMT has direct HBM and AI OSAT order evidence and belongs in the underfollowed discovery lane as an inspection/metrology bottleneck candidate.
FORM has direct HBM test evidence through probe-card products, SK hynix recognition, and Q1 2026 DRAM/HBM demand commentary; it is a strong Layer 1B test-node candidate.

KLIC is a plausible but less proven advanced-packaging equipment candidate; thesis requires proof that TCB, APTURA, vertical wire, memory, and heterogeneous integration products are becoming material HBM/AI revenue drivers.

The node is best mapped into four investable public-market subnodes: OSAT capacity, HBM/advanced-package inspection and metrology, HBM wafer/stack probe cards, and advanced bonding/interconnect equipment.

Need a later layer to add non-US primary listings or ADR/OTC-accessible Taiwan/Korea/Japan names such as Powertech-like OSATs, substrate suppliers, test-handler vendors, and consumables suppliers; this pass was constrained to US-listed companies.

node: HBM, advanced packaging, OSAT, and backend memory-test overflow
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around HBM and advanced-packaging overflow capacity. The cleanest direct exposures found in this pass are not the obvious HBM producers or AI accelerator customers, but US-listed OSAT, advanced-packaging equipment, probe-card/test, and inspection/metrology companies. Amkor is the reference OSAT anchor; Camtek and FormFactor have direct HBM-related order/product evidence; Kulicke & Soffa is a more indirect advanced-packaging equipment name tied to thermocompression bonding, heterogeneous integration, CPO, and memory/high-compute packaging. These are research candidates only, not recommendations.
